about: Labelled page-level corpus for the unusable-text-layer detector (PLA-148).
Each case is one page's extracted text, labelled by whether Lyra should treat that
text layer as usable. `usable` means the extracted text is worth indexing; `unusable`
means the page should be dropped and sent to the recognition flow instead, because
indexing its text would retrieve words the page does not say.
`category` groups cases by the failure (or non-failure) they exercise. `detectable`
records whether the shipped signals claim to catch the category from text alone: the
detector is tuned for precision, so a few genuinely hard pathologies - reordered
columns, a coherent unrelated overlay, scattered equation glyphs - are labelled
unusable but marked `detectable: false`, and the harness reports them as known false
negatives rather than chasing them with a rule that would drop valid pages.
The text is written rather than scraped: a corpus of a student's own documents cannot
be committed, and tuning to one course's real files would overfit the thresholds to
that course's formatting. `photographed` pages are covered by a separate rendered
fixture in backend/tests/test_parse.py, because that gate needs the page image.

cases.name: prose-linear-algebra
cases.label: usable
cases.text: The determinant of a triangular matrix is the product of the entries on its main diagonal. This follows from the cofactor expansion along the first column, where every term below the diagonal contributes a zero. As a consequence, a triangular matrix is invertible exactly when none of its diagonal entries is zero, and its inverse is again triangular of the same kind.

cases.name: prose-lecture-note
cases.label: usable
cases.text: Today we introduce the notion of a limit. Intuitively, a function approaches a limit as its input approaches some value when the outputs cluster arbitrarily close to a single number. We will make this precise using the epsilon-delta definition, and then use it to prove that continuous functions are closed under addition and composition.

cases.name: prose-definition-theorem
cases.label: usable
cases.text: Definition. A sequence converges to a limit L if for every positive epsilon there exists an index beyond which every term lies within epsilon of L. Theorem. Every convergent sequence is bounded. The proof takes epsilon equal to one and observes that all but finitely many terms lie in a bounded interval, while the finitely many remaining terms are bounded on their own.

cases.name: theorem-with-formulas
cases.label: usable
cases.text: Theorem 3.1. Let A be an n by n matrix. Then det(AB) = det(A) det(B). Proof. Both sides are multilinear alternating functions of the columns of B, and they agree on the identity, so they agree everywhere. QED. Corollary. det(A^{-1}) = 1/det(A) whenever A is invertible.
